newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says Schiphol night take-off ban unacceptable.
newsitem.headline: KLM says Schiphol night take-off ban unacceptable.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Friday a ban by Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport on freighter departures at night was "unacceptable."

The Amsterdam airport authority said on Friday take-off was banned between 2300 and 0600 on McDonnell Douglas DC-10 aircraft and the Boeing 747 in its 100,200, 300 and SP versions from August 1, in a bid to cut back on noise pollution.

Schiphol's proposals have to be agreed by the Dutch government, while the airport authority's president Hans Smits told a news conference that KLM had indicated its fleet mix could cope with the noise restrictions without undue disruption.
KLM, the national Dutch carrier, will be sending a counter-proposal to the Dutch government calling for an exemption for quieter aircraft.

"We have studied the Schiphol proposal and are unpleasantly surprised," the KLM spokesman said. "We have been in talks with the airport over the last month in an effort to reach an acceptable solution to the noise problems.

"KLM considers that these measures represent an overkill of the noise problems and this is unacceptable," he stressed. He said the restrictions were unacceptable "both operationally and commercially."
Boeing 747-200s and 300s can be considered as quieter aircraft depending on their take-off weight and engine equipment, he added.
U.S. carrier, Atlas Air, operates Boeing 747-200 freighters on behalf of KLM Cargo and three of these flights a week will be hit by the new ban, said the spokesman.
He said these aircraft qualify as quieter aircraft because of the type of engines with which they are fitted.

Another worry the airline has concerns its Boeing 747-300 Combi fleet. "If one of these aircraft is scheduled to depart at 2245 hours and gets a short delay, does it have to remain at the airport all night?"
KLM will be sending its counter-proposal to the Dutch government this afternoon or Monday July 14, he said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
